id_connor_columns.blurb: Connor Columns is a small cliff of columnar volcanic rock in south-central Idaho, on a hillside reached by dirt road north of the village of Connor. It is almost entirely a trad crag: of 16 listed climbs, 14 are trad and two are bolted, spanning easy 5.6 terrain up to a few 5.11s and one 5.12 line, with the bulk between 5.7 and 5.10. Expect splitter hand cracks, fairly clean crack systems and face holds on a wall roughly twenty metres tall. It faces southwest and gets sun for much of the day. The walk in is a scrubby bushwhack, and rattlesnakes are common, so watch your step.

id_03_the_snarl.blurb: The Snarl is one of the sub-crags of The Nose, in the Teddy Bear Cove sport area of southeast Idaho near American Falls. Its 16 routes are nearly all bolted sport lines with a single top-rope problem, running from 5.9 up to a lone route in the low 5.12 range, with most landing at 5.10 and 5.11. The basalt tends to get steeper and cleaner as you move along the wall, and the quality is generally good. The face leans toward the west, and many lines sit close to a large juniper tree. The cove as a whole is known as a warm option for cooler months.

id_fence_line.blurb: Fence Line is a granite formation in the East Sector of Castle Rocks, near Almo in southern Idaho. It holds 16 mostly single-pitch routes, twelve of them trad and four sport. Difficulty starts near 5.5 and is concentrated in the 5.6 to 5.8 range, with a handful of harder lines including a 5.10 and a 5.12 test piece, which makes it a pleasant place for moderate climbers. Faces point south, east and west, so you can choose sun or shade to suit the day. The rock is good, and there is a small summit on top. A trail leads to each face from the main road.

id_ivy_league_wall.blurb: Ivy League Wall is the far southern end of the Sunny Side cliffs at Ross Park in Pocatello. It has 16 climbs, mostly short bolted sport routes plus a couple of top-rope lines, from about 5.6 to the low 5.12s with most between 5.8 and 5.10. The basalt faces southwest and heats up in summer afternoons, so locals shift to shadier walls once the sun arrives. It sees comparatively little traffic. Poison ivy once gave the wall its name and a few plants may still lurk at the base and on the approach. The walk from the dirt lot is brief.
id_ivy_league_wall.approach: From the dirt lot, follow the dirt road below the cliff bands to its south end, then take the short trail up to the wall.

id_post_wall.blurb: Post Wall is a sport wall at Q'Emiln Park in Post Falls, North Idaho, close to the Spokane River. All 16 routes are bolted, and several can also be top-roped. Grades run from 5.7 to 5.11, and the bulk sit at 5.10, so it suits climbers working through that grade. Trees keep the wall mostly shaded through the day and it faces west. Reach it by following the river trail around the bluff and down a natural staircase. The park as a whole offers vertical, positive-holds gneiss and short approaches.

id_outlaw_wall.blurb: Outlaw Wall is a less-traveled cliff at Q'Emiln Park in Post Falls, North Idaho, mixing eight sport routes, three trad lines and five boulder problems. Routes range from around 5.6 to 5.11, with the majority near 5.9, and the boulders run V1 to V3. Most lines face southwest to west: belays stay shaded, while the upper wall catches afternoon and evening sun. The approach descends a steep hill with some easy downclimbing before following trails along the rim, so bring a map. Traffic is light.

id_lower_ledge_area.blurb: Lower Ledge Area is a popular cliff for moderate climbers at Q'Emiln Park in Post Falls, North Idaho, and the first one you meet on the stairway trail down from the entrance. It has 15 climbs: eight sport, six trad and a top-rope line, from an easy 5.4 crack up to a 5.12, with a good cluster of 5.10s and plenty at 5.7 to 5.9. The face is in full sun by mid-morning on most days and gets very hot in summer, so it is a better pick for cooler weather. The park's rock is vertical gneiss with positive holds.

id_taj_mahal_the.blurb: The Taj Mahal is a cluster of basalt boulders in the Swan Falls bouldering area, on the east bank of the Snake River south of Boise. The blocks top out around twelve feet, so the problems are low enough for a pad-and-spotter approach. There are 15 problems, from V0 through V7, with a spread of easy, mid-grade and hard lines; the hardest are several V6s and a V7. There is no tree shade, and the canyon walls block morning sun, so spring, autumn and winter suit it best.
